newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-TEST TURNS IN NZ'S FAVOUR VS SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TEST TURNS IN NZ'S FAVOUR VS SRI LANKA.

text.p: A test-best performance by reformed fast bowler Heath Davis fired New Zealand into a strong position at the close of the second day of the second cricket test against Sri Lanka on Saturday.
The Wellington paceman collected five for 63 in just his fourth test to help roll the tourists for 170 and earn his side a first innings advantage of 52 runs on a rapidly wearing pitch.
New Zealand then extended their lead to 105 at the close when they were 53 for one in their second innings, with Bryan Young unbeaten on 22 and Matt Horne on 10.
They lost opening batsman Blair Pocock for seven in the sixth over when he edged a ball from left arm seamer Nuwan Zoysa to Roshan Mahanama at second slip.
Young was fortunate to survive -- he was dropped on six at slip by Mahanama from the first delivery bowled by offspinner Kumar Dharmasena.
New Zealand won the first test in Dunedin earlier this week by an innings and 36 runs, and need only to draw this game to secure their first series victory in more than four years.
But a drawn result looks out of the question with 21 wickets having already fallen in six sessions.
The career of Davis, once rated by former New Zealand batsman and English county player Roger Twose as the fastest white bowler in the world, had been plagued by a lack of control.
He played one test in England in 1994 and was then ignored by the New Zealand selectors until the third test against the Englishmen in Christchurch last month.
Davis, who now bowls within himself and subsequently adheres to a tighter line, and teenaged left arm spinner Daniel Vettori caused the damage for New Zealand.

Vettori, just 18 and appearing in a test for just the fourth time, chipped in with four for 46 from 25 accurate overs on a surface causing problems and which is unlikely to see the match go the full distance of five days.
He relished playing on his home ground to display good control and flight in the air and again underline the the big role he may play in the resurgence of the New Zealand team.

Opener Mahanama topscored for the tourists with a diligent 45 while lower order batsmen Chaminda Vaas, with 28, and Kumar Dharmasena, with 27, put their heads down to grind out a seventh wicket stand of 53 in two hours.
Aravinda de Silva's dismal series continued when he made just one to lift his run aggregate from his last three innings to four before Vettori captured his first wicket of the innings this morning.
